subject: Logic
title: Universal Quantifier
description: Learn Universal Quantifier in one minute.

hook.text: "Every student passed." In symbols: ∀x (S(x) → P(x)). The upside-down A means "for all."

buildup.text: The universal quantifier (∀) asserts that a property holds for every member of a domain.

discovery.text: ∀x P(x) is true only if P(x) is true for every single x. One exception makes it false.

twist.text: The domain matters enormously. "All numbers are positive" is false for integers but true for natural numbers.

climax.text: Universal statements are bold claims. They're easy to disprove—just find one counterexample.
